ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Let \( g(t) = (1+t)u(t) \) represent the impulse response of a linear, time-invariant system that is part of the feedback system shown in the image. The number of zeros of the closed-loop transfer function \( \frac{Y}{X} \) is:
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, input X enters the summing node on the left, and the input end is marked with a positive sign; a feedback branch is split from output Y, passes through a feedback block with gain 4, and then returns to the negative-sign end of the summing node. Therefore the image represents a standard negative feedback system, the forward path is an LTI system represented by impulse response g(t)=(1+t)u(t), and the feedback gain is 4. Then reason: The forward transfer function G(s) is the Laplace transform of g(t), namely G(s)=L{(1+t)u(t)}=1/s+1/s^2=(s+1)/s^2. The negative-feedback closed-loop transfer function is T(s)=Y(s)/X(s)=G(s)/(1+4G(s)). Substituting gives T(s)=((s+1)/s^2)/(1+4(s+1)/s^2)=(s+1)/(s^2+4s+4)=(s+1)/(s+2)^2. The numerator s+1 has one root s=-1 that has not been canceled, so the closed-loop transfer function has 1 zero.

Substitute into T(s)=G(s)/(1+4G(s)) and simplify: T(s)=(s+1)/(s^2+4s+4)=(s+1)/(s+2)^2. Since the numerator has one uncancelled root, conclude the closed-loop transfer function has 1 zero.
